description: Host your Minecraft world through Steam lobbies and play with Steam friends: no port forwarding, just Steam's P2P relay.

releases.notes:
Steamed now runs on **Minecraft 1.20.1**, on Fabric and on Forge.

### New

- **Minecraft 1.20.1** on Fabric and **Forge** (Forge 47.x, the loader most 1.20.1 modpacks use). Hosting, the lobby
  screen, invites, the friends' lobbies list and the title-screen and pause-menu buttons work the same as on 1.21.1
  and 26.2

| Jar | Minecraft | Also needs |
|---|---|---|
| `steamed-fabric-0.2.1+26.2.jar` | 26.2 | Fabric API, Fabric Language Kotlin |
| `steamed-neoforge-0.2.1+26.2.jar` | 26.2 | Kotlin for Forge 6.4+ |
| `steamed-quilt-0.2.1+26.2.jar` | 26.2 | Fabric API, Fabric Language Kotlin |
| `steamed-fabric-0.2.1+1.21.1.jar` | 1.21, 1.21.1 | Fabric API, Fabric Language Kotlin |
| `steamed-neoforge-0.2.1+1.21.1.jar` | 1.21.1 | Kotlin for Forge 5.12+ |
| `steamed-fabric-0.2.1+1.20.1.jar` | 1.20.1 | Fabric API, Fabric Language Kotlin |
| `steamed-forge-0.2.1+1.20.1.jar` | 1.20.1 | Kotlin for Forge 4.12+ |

### Fixes

- The invite screen showed each friend's Steam status as a raw code name (`LookingToPlay`) and always said
  "(invited)" in English. Both are translated now, into every language Steamed ships

### Good to know

- 1.20.1, 1.21.1 and 26.2 players can't join each other. The friends' lobbies list greys out a lobby from a different
  Minecraft version and says why
- Not on 1.20.1: Quilt, NeoForge (barely used on 1.20.1), and player heads inside chat lines (join and leave lines still
  get the orange diamond)
- Joining a friend, kicking, voice chat and web maps across two Steam accounts haven't been tested on 1.20.1 yet
- Everyone in a lobby still needs the same Steamed version, so update together with your friends

Steamed now runs on **Minecraft 1.21.1** as well as 26.2.

### New

- **Minecraft 1.21.1** (and 1.21), on Fabric and NeoForge. Hosting, the lobby screen, invites, the friends' lobbies
  list and the title-screen and pause-menu buttons all work the same as on 26.2
- One jar per Minecraft version and loader, named like `steamed-fabric-0.2.0+1.21.1.jar`. Pick the one that matches
  your game:

| Jar | Minecraft | Also needs |
|---|---|---|
| `steamed-fabric-0.2.0+26.2.jar` | 26.2 | Fabric API, Fabric Language Kotlin |
| `steamed-neoforge-0.2.0+26.2.jar` | 26.2 | Kotlin for Forge 6.4+ |
| `steamed-quilt-0.2.0+26.2.jar` | 26.2 | Fabric API, Fabric Language Kotlin |
| `steamed-fabric-0.2.0+1.21.1.jar` | 1.21, 1.21.1 | Fabric API, Fabric Language Kotlin |
| `steamed-neoforge-0.2.0+1.21.1.jar` | 1.21.1 | Kotlin for Forge 5.12+ |

### Changes

- The invite screen draws each friend's face next to their name instead of inside it
- Behind the scenes, every version and loader is now built from one source tree, so later backports are much cheaper

### Good to know

- 1.21.1 and 26.2 players can't join each other. The friends' lobbies list greys out a lobby from a different
  Minecraft version and says why
- Not on 1.21.1: Quilt, and player heads inside chat lines (join and leave lines still get the orange diamond)
- Verified on 1.21.1 so far: loading, connecting to Steam, the title screen and joining a world, on both loaders.
  Joining a friend, kicking, voice chat and web maps across two Steam accounts haven't been tested on 1.21.1 yet
- Everyone in a lobby still needs the same Steamed version, so update together with your friends

A fix release for NeoForge: Steamed 0.1.3 crashed at startup on a real NeoForge install.

### Fixes

- **NeoForge:** the 0.1.3 jar crashed while loading, first because nothing provided Kotlin, then because Steam's native
  libraries were loaded where Steamed couldn't reach them. Both are fixed, and NeoForge now starts, connects to Steam
  and hosts lobbies
- Steam's native libraries are now loaded by Steamed itself on every loader, instead of through LWJGL

### Good to know

- **NeoForge now needs [Kotlin for Forge](https://modrinth.com/mod/kotlin-for-forge)** (6.4.0 or newer). NeoForge
  tells you if it's missing, and the Modrinth app installs it for you
- The Fabric and Quilt jars still need Fabric API and Fabric Language Kotlin
- 0.1.3 and 0.1.4 can play together; nothing about the connection changed

The first public release of Steamed: host your Minecraft world through a Steam lobby and play with your Steam friends,
with no port forwarding and no third-party tunnels. Connections go through Steam's own peer-to-peer network, directly
when possible and relayed when not.

Install the jar for your loader (Fabric, NeoForge or Quilt) and keep Steam running. Everyone in a lobby needs Steamed
0.1.3 and the same Minecraft version.

### Hosting and joining

- Create a lobby from the pause menu, then invite friends from an in-game friend list (no Steam overlay needed)
- Invites show up as a toast and wait for you to accept them
- The Steam Lobby screen lists friends who are hosting right now, so you can join without an invite
- Lobbies are friends-only or invite-only, with a max players setting (2, 4, 8, 16 or 250). Lobbies above 8 work because
  Steamed lifts the integrated server's built-in 8-player cap while you host
- Hosts can kick players. Everyone is disconnected cleanly when the host closes the lobby

### Security

- Every joiner proves who they are with a Steam auth ticket before any traffic reaches your world
- A world hosted through Steam is only opened on loopback, not to your LAN
- If e4mc or e4all is installed, Steamed warns that it may also have opened your world to the internet

### Extras

- Simple Voice Chat and Plasmo Voice are tunnelled through Steam automatically
- BlueMap and squaremap web maps reach joiners through Steam, with a chat link to open them
- Players who joined through Steam get an orange diamond before their name tag and in the Tab list, and their
  join/leave lines in chat are orange too
- Player heads for Steam friends in the lobby and invite screens

### Quality of life

- Translated into English, Polish, German, Ukrainian and Russian
- Steam not running is handled: a toast at startup, and a retry button in the lobby screen once you've started Steam.
  If Steam quits mid-game, you leave the lobby cleanly and are told why
- Lobbies record Minecraft's version, so hosts on a different version are greyed out instead of failing mid-connect

### Good to know

- Steamed uses Spacewar (Steam app ID 480) for now, so friends see you as "playing Spacewar"
- Quilt support is experimental
- The Fabric and Quilt jars need Fabric API and Fabric Language Kotlin. NeoForge needs nothing else
